source.credit: Buie et al. (2015), The Astronomical Journal 149, 113; existing JPL#82 Patroclus-Menoetius source closure

constraints.axisConvention: Full axes are halved exactly. +Z is the adopted pole; +X is the arbitrary display meridian.
constraints.qualification: Published primary-component ellipsoid combining occultation and light-curve constraints. Its full axes differ from the two-dimensional occultation limb and from the unresolved binary system's radiometric diameter.
constraints.scale: The reference radius is the geometric mean of the approximation semiaxes. It is a rendering scale, not an independent measured mean radius or convex-model volume.

assumptions: Published primary-component ellipsoid combining occultation and light-curve constraints. Its full axes differ from the two-dimensional occultation limb and from the unresolved binary system's radiometric diameter.
Synchronous spin-axis approximation using the same 2024 orbital pole as Menoetius; arbitrary display meridian. A physical mutual-event phase is not claimed.
approximation.qualification: Observation-constrained ellipsoid; no invented local terrain or albedo.

spin.meaning: Synchronous spin-axis approximation using the same 2024 orbital pole as Menoetius; arbitrary display meridian. A physical mutual-event phase is not claimed.

unresolved: Local shape deviations and a physical mutual-event rotational phase remain unqualified.
The existing Menoetius package supplies the retained primary-specific heliocentric state; the system barycentre is not substituted for Patroclus.
